subject: DeepCart renewal & usage ROI benchmark sync
messages:
From: Elena Park <ep@deepcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage & renewal numbers ahead of Q3

Hi Marissa,

Hope you had a good weekend. We’re starting internal planning for Q3 renewal conversations and I wanted to get a clean break-down of our Q2 token consumption and any performance outliers (latency/errors) before we commit to terms. Specifically: 

- Token spend by feature (chat, embeddings, reranking) for May–June.
- Peak latency incidents and root-cause notes (we had a couple user reports last month).
- Any quick wins on cost per token you recommend (quantization, batching, caching).

We’re evaluating two directions: 1) simple committed tokens with a standard discount, or 2) a short Dedicated pilot (2–3 GPUs) for high-volume inference paths. The pilot would help us stabilize tail latency and reduce unit cost if the numbers line up.

Attached is our ops export if that helps (DeepCart_Q2_ops_log.csv). Can you share a short ROI summary and a recommendation by next Wednesday (Jul 13)? I’m also happy to jump on a 30-min call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform
DeepCart
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <ep@deepcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage & renewal numbers ahead of Q3

Elena — thanks for the note and for the ops export. High level summary up front:

- Q2 token spend (May 1–Jun 30): ~56M tokens total. Breakdown: chat 68% (~38M), embeddings 18% (~10M), rerank/other 14% (~8M).
- Cost profile: blended unit cost today ~$0.0009/token (hosted, mixed model mix).
- Spikes & latency: two notable incidents on 2028-06-12 (regional GPU contention) and 2028-06-24 (gateway timeout during a marketing surge). Median tail latency at peak ~1.8s; 95th percentile spiked to 6–8s during the incidents.

Recommended path (short): 12-month committed tier + 60-day Dedicated pilot focused on chat threads with high concurrency. Expected outcomes: ~18–28% unit-cost reduction from batching + KV caching + a quantized model option, and 40–60% reduction in 95th percentile latency for the pilot traffic slice.

Attached: DeepCart_Q2_usage_report.pdf (summary deck) and a renewal_playbook.xlsx with three commit tiers and projected savings. Quick numbers from the playbook:
- Option A (12mo, 20% commit): 10% discount, blended cost ~$0.00081/token.
- Option B (12mo, 40% commit + pilot): 15% discount + pilot savings = blended ~$0.00066/token.
- Option C (24mo preferred, staged): 18% discount, best economics but longer lock-in.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want the Dedicated pilot, we’ll scope an objectives doc and SLOs (latency/availability/throughput).
2) If you prefer committed tokens, we’ll send a formal pricing term sheet and include a one-time migration/ops credit to offset the spike risk.

I’m available Wed afternoon for a 30-min sync. Ben (cc’d) has a short technical note on cache strategy that I’ve asked to include.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Park <ep@deepcart.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage & renewal numbers ahead of Q3 (technical notes)

Elena / Marissa — quick technical addendum to Marissa’s summary. TL;DR: we can target the biggest wins without a full model retrain.

- Caching: Prefix/KV caching for chat histories will cut repeated-token compute on stateful flows; for DeepCart we estimate ~11–16% token reduction on active sessions (your export shows a lot of repeated product-context prompts).
- Batching: Controlled concurrent batching at the gateway for non-interactive embeddings/rerank jobs can reduce per-token GPU overhead ~12–18% with minimal latency impact when applied to background workloads.
- Quantization/variants: Running a quantized 4-bit variant for non-sensitive embedding workloads reduces memory footprint and can unlock denser packing on Dedicated. We can run an AB test during the pilot for quality checks.
- Incident notes: 2028-06-12 was correlated with multi-tenant GPU contention at a single AZ; we recommended routing policy changes then which avoided recurrence. For the 06-24 surge, we propose a short-term burst lane for known campaign windows (pre-provisioned capacity) and a longer-term Dedicated pilot for predictable high concurrency.

Estimated blended unit-cost improvement if you adopt pilot + caching + batching: 22–28% (range depends on adoption of caching for chat). We’ll provide a small eval harness to validate inference latency and token savings on your sample traces.

Attachments referenced in Marissa’s deck include suggested SLOs and a draft pilot runbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Park <ep@deepcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage & renewal numbers ahead of Q3 — proposed terms

Elena — thanks for the context and everyone for the analysis. I reviewed Marissa’s playbook and Ben’s technical note. I’m comfortable moving forward with Option B (12-month, 40% commit + 60-day Dedicated pilot focused on chat concurrency). A few operational asks before we finalize:

1) Marissa: please send the formal term sheet with the 15% price discount and pilot scope (objectives + SLOs) to accounts@deepcart.com and loop in Redwood Finance.
2) Ben: include the pilot runbook (traffic slice, AB test plan for quantized variant, and a short rollback plan).
3) Legal/Finance: we’ll include a one-time migration credit to cover two incident windows historically and an SLA commitment for 95th percentile latency during pilot.

Elena — if this sounds good I’ll sign off on the commercial side once Finance confirms the numbers. Marissa, can you aim to get the term sheet over by EOD Wed Jul 18?

Karthik
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
